subject: project:gdl
value: CODEGEN LAW, and the price tag on every own-pool-ghost cleanup: REPLACING AN `extern fN lbl_ADDR` READ WITH THE EQUIVALENT LITERAL IS NOT CODEGEN-NEUTRAL. The standing framing (attempt.EO_enemy-c-data-claims-land-two-of-three-...20260904.v1's hypothesis.count_consequence, quoted verbatim: 'count-neutral for .text: replacing a named-extern constant read with a literal keeps the same instruction word and changes only the relocation's symbol') is HALF TRUE. The instruction COUNT half holds -- measured over all 66 functions of game/enemy/enemy across a 74-symbol / 323-site conversion, not one function changed its instruction count. The 'same instruction word' half is FALSE: TWELVE of the 66 changed instruction WORDS. MECHANISM. MWCC treats a read of an extern scalar as an opaque memory reference it must respect -- it cannot rematerialise the value, cannot hoist it across a store, and must keep it live in a register or spill it. The same value spelled as a literal is a pool constant the compiler owns: it may reload it anywhere for free, reassociate around it, and schedule its load independently. Removing that barrier moves register pressure. MEASURED SHAPES, all from one build pair (the un-postprocessed body object at HEAD versus the converted source, instruction words only): (a) FRAME GROWTH in seven functions -- closest_enemy `stwu r1,-192(r1)` -> `-200(r1)` with `stmw r23,84(r1)` -> `92(r1)`, do_enemy_move -208 -> -224, do_enemy_collide -136 -> -144, fn_80045C30 -152 -> -168, fn_8004646C -208 -> -216, fn_8004DC2C -32 -> -40, find_enemy_slot -24 -> -48; (b) POOL LOAD RESCHEDULED AHEAD OF A STRUCT LOAD with the two FPR roles exchanged, in move_logic06 (x3), move_logic14, damage_enemy and fn_8004DC2C -- `lfs f1,588(r31); lfd f0,0(0)` becomes `lfd f1,0(0); lfs f0,588(r31)`; (c) COMMUTATIVE OPERAND SWAP in fn_8004DF58 -- `fmul f31,f31,f0` becomes `fmul f31,f0,f31` (x2); (d) a pure FPR RECOLOR in move_logic22. Against the target the conversion cost +134 raw differing words TU-wide and took the byte-exact function count from 45 to 39. THE EFFECT IS NOT CONCENTRATED: a variant that held all 73 other conversions fixed and kept only the single most-referenced non-const extern (lbl_80346820, f32 0.0, 39 sites) still moved ELEVEN functions. TWO CONSEQUENCES. (1) An own-pool-ghost cleanup on a TU with matched functions is MATCHING WORK, not hygiene, and must be gated on a word-for-word body-object comparison, never on `real` (which claim.law.own-pool-ghost-extern-flatters-fndiff-reloc-rows.20260831.v1 already shows is defined to worsen) and never on the compile succeeding. (2) STRING externs are exempt in .sdata2 and NOT exempt in .rodata: converting 18 `extern char lbl_80346xxx[]` string ghosts to literals in game/game/gamemain (44 sites, .sdata2 0x58 -> 0xBF) moved ZERO of 77 functions, while converting six `.rodata` string ghosts in the same TU (7 sites) moved init_next_level_8005638C -- and BOTH disjoint halves of that six moved the SAME function, so it is adding anything at all to that TU's .rodata that does it, not any particular string.
